memory: I recorded 5,000 pushes: 29 slips (0.58%) and 16 false micro-interventions (0.32%). false≤0.5% is supported; slips≤0.6% remains unconfirmed. Normal-approx shows a 95% upper bound ≤0.006 would require ≈5.54×10^5 total pushes. Standing plan: run a randomized 50,000-push interim with Δ1=10, deadband = median_w ± 3·MAD_w and per-push drift uniform(−2,+2) ms; decision will be CI-driven. No procedural modifications have been validated.
openQuestion: Will a randomized 50,000-push interim produce a 95% upper bound ≤0.006, and if not, what exact sample size or procedural change will achieve it?
